name: @agenticdevelopertoolkit/themes
description: Theme manifest, ThemeStyle component, and ColorModeProvider for agenticdevelopertoolkit.
comment:files: `src/styles` + `src/tailwind.css` ship ALONGSIDE dist: the `./styles/*.css` and `./tailwind.css` exports resolve to `./src/...` unconditionally (prod too), and `pnpm deploy`/`npm pack` only include listed paths, so any package exporting raw CSS instead of bundling it into JS must list its `src/...` paths in `files` explicitly — omitting one silently breaks that export for anyone installing from a tarball.
comment:exports: `development` → src for `next dev` (HMR, no build/restart); prod (NODE_ENV=production) skips it → dist, which is self-degrading if a bundler doesn't understand the `development` condition — it just falls back to the unconditional `import` key. NOTE: src/theme-data.ts is generated by `build:data` — it must exist for the dev (src) path; `postinstall` runs it, so any workspace that links this package (including a consumer linking it from a submodule) gets it on install.
comment:exports:./materialize-fonts: Unconditionally src, and NOT a tsup entry: its three callers are all a next.config, which runs before the bundler exists and imports it by relative PATH (see the module's own header). The export is there for anyone who can resolve the package normally, so the path form stays an implementation detail of the two places that cannot. This note sits OUT here rather than beside the entry because node's resolver rejects an `exports` object that mixes subpath keys with non-subpath ones — ERR_INVALID_PACKAGE_CONFIG on EVERY import of the package, not just that one. Bundlers only warn, so a test suite stays green through it.

scripts.build: pnpm run build:tokens && pnpm run build:data && tsup && pnpm run build:types && pnpm run build:css
scripts.dev: pnpm run build:tokens && pnpm run build:data && tsup --watch
